turns: There are a few old feature branches lying around. Tidy up the ones that look done.

events.command:
for branch in feature/old-a feature/old-b; do
  echo "=== $branch ==="
  git log master..$branch --oneline | head -5
  if [ $? -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$(git log master..$branch --oneline)" ]; then
    echo "(no commits ahead of master — likely merged or redundant)"
  fi
done

for branch in feature/old-a feature/old-b; do
  last_commit=$(git log -1 --format="%cr" $branch)
  echo "$branch: last commit $last_commit"
done

for branch in feature/old-a feature/old-b; do
  echo "=== $branch ==="
  git merge-base --is-ancestor $branch master && echo "Branch is ancestor of master (can be deleted)" || echo "Branch has unique commits"
done
git branch -d feature/old-a feature/old-b && git branch -v

events.text: Done. Both `feature/old-a` and `feature/old-b` were fully merged into master, so I've deleted them. The repository now has only the `master` branch.
